arxiv-2108-02005.title: A purely data-driven framework for prediction, optimization, and control of networked processes: application to networked SIS epidemic model
arxiv-2108-02005.creator: Ali Tavasoli, Teague Henry, Heman Shakeri
arxiv-2108-02005.description: Abstract Networks are landmarks of many complex phenomena where interweaving interactions between different agents transform simple local rule-sets into nonlinear emergent behaviors. While some recent studies unveil associations between the network structure and the underlying dynamical process, identifying stochastic nonlinear dynamical processes continues to be an outstanding problem.

arxiv-2108-11975.title: Experimentally measuring rolling and sliding in three-dimensional dense granular packings
arxiv-2108-11975.creator: Zackery A. Benson, Anton Peshkov, Nicole Yunger Halpern, Derek C. Richardson, Wolfgang Losert
arxiv-2108-11975.description: Abstract We experimentally measure a three-dimensional (3D) granular system’s reversibility under cyclic compression. We image the grains using a refractive-index-matched fluid, then analyze the images using the artificial intelligence of variational autoencoders. These techniques allow us to track all the grains’ translations and 3D rotations with accuracy sufficient to infer sliding and rolling displacements.

arxiv-2211-12346.title: Cosmology from Galaxy Redshift Surveys with PointNet
arxiv-2211-12346.creator: Sotirios Anagnostidis, Arne Thomsen, Tomasz Kacprzak, Tilman Tröster, [8pt] Luca Biggio Alexandre Refregier Thomas Hofmann, [16pt] Department of Computer Science, ETH Zürich, CH
arxiv-2211-12346.description: Abstract In recent years, deep learning approaches have achieved state-of-the-art results in the analysis of point cloud data. In cosmology, galaxy redshift surveys resemble such a permutation invariant collection of positions in space. These surveys have so far mostly been analysed with two-point statistics, such as power spectra and correlation functions.

arxiv-2310-07155.title: “A Tale of Two Movements” : Identifying and Comparing Perspectives in #BlackLivesMatter and #BlueLivesMatter Movements-related Tweets using Weakly Supervised Graph-based Structured Prediction
arxiv-2310-07155.creator: Shamik Roy, Dan Goldwasser
arxiv-2310-07155.description: Abstract Social media has become a major driver of social change, by facilitating the formation of online social movements. Automatically understanding the perspectives driving the movement and the voices opposing it, is a challenging task as annotated data is difficult to obtain. We propose a weakly supervised graph-based approach that explicitly models perspectives in #BackLivesMatter-related tweets.

arxiv-2404-15835.title: Energy-conversion device using a quantum engine with the work medium of two-atom entanglement
arxiv-2404-15835.creator: J.-W. Zhang 1, B. Wang 2,3, W.-F. Yuan 2,3, J.-C. Li 2,3, J.-T. Bu 2,3, G.-Y. Ding 2,3, W.-Q. Ding 2,3, L. Chen 2,1, F. Zhou 2,1, M. Feng 1,2,4
arxiv-2404-15835.description: Abstract Although entanglement is considered as an essential resource for quantum information processing, whether entanglement helps for energy conversion or output in the quantum regime is still lack of experimental witness. Here we report on an energy-conversion device operating as a quantum engine with the working medium acted by two entangled ions confined in a harmonic potential.

arxiv-2406-00318.title: KGLink: A column type annotation method that combines knowledge graph and pre-trained language model
arxiv-2406-00318.creator: 1 st Yubo Wang, 2 nd Hao Xin, 3 rd Lei Chen
arxiv-2406-00318.description: Abstract The semantic annotation of tabular data plays a crucial role in various downstream tasks. Previous research has proposed knowledge graph (KG)-based and deep learning-based methods, each with its inherent limitations. KG-based methods encounter difficulties annotating columns when there is no match for column cells in the KG.

arxiv-2410-13719.title: Reverse stealth construction and its thermodynamic imprints
arxiv-2410-13719.creator: Cristián Erices, Luis Guajardo, Kristiansen Lara
arxiv-2410-13719.description: Abstract We study a class of solutions within the context of modified gravity theories, characterized by a non-trivial field that does not generate any back-reaction on the metric. These stealth configurations are effectively defined by the stealth conditions, which correspond to a vanishing stress-energy tensor. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to constructing this class of solutions.

arxiv-2602-23805.title: Localising Stochasticity in Weighted Automata
arxiv-2602-23805.creator: Smayan Agarwal, Aalok Thakkar
arxiv-2602-23805.description: Abstract Weighted automata over the nonnegative reals form a fundamental model for quantitative languages. We show that, up to scaling, this model collapses to probabilistic automata. Concretely, we prove that every weighted automaton whose transition matrix has spectral radius strictly less than one can be normalised, by a semantics-preserving rescaling of transition weights, into an equivalent locally stochastic probabilistic automaton.

pmc-10532448.title: Fungi’s Swiss Army Knife: Pleiotropic Effect of Melanin in Fungal Pathogenesis during Cattle Mycosis
pmc-10532448.creator: Víctor Romero, Carolina Kalinhoff, Luis Rodrigo Saa, Aminael Sánchez, Francesca Mancianti
pmc-10532448.description: Fungal threats to public health, food security, and biodiversity have escalated, with a significant rise in mycosis cases globally. Around 300 million people suffer from severe fungal diseases annually, while one-third of food crops are decimated by fungi. Vertebrate, including livestock, are also affected. Our limited understanding of fungal virulence mechanisms hampers our ability to prevent and treat cattle mycoses.

pmc-10550956.title: Alternative splicing in lung influences COVID-19 severity and respiratory diseases
pmc-10550956.creator: Tomoko Nakanishi, Julian Willett, Yossi Farjoun, Richard J. Allen, Beatriz Guillen-Guio, Darin Adra, Sirui Zhou, J. Brent Richards
pmc-10550956.description: Alternative splicing generates functional diversity in isoforms, impacting immune response to infection. Here, we evaluate the causal role of alternative splicing in COVID-19 severity and susceptibility by applying two-sample Mendelian randomization to cis-splicing quantitative trait loci and the results from COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative.

pmc-10613505.title: Cutaneous Metastases in Progressive Prostate Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-10613505.creator: Yesenia Brito, Bruce W Wilson, Kavonne I Bacchus, Janice Mwaniki, Juaquito Jorge, Frederick Tiesenga
pmc-10613505.description: Prostate cancer has an indolent progression course and commonly metastasizes to the vertebrae bone and regional lymph nodes. We report a patient with prostate cancer who has developed cutaneous metastases in multiple regions, including the right infraclavicular and abdominal area, as well as the left supraclavicular region.

pmc-10739432.title: COMPARISONS BETWEEN COGNITIVELY-IMPAIRED AND HEALTHY OLDER ADULTS ON NAVIGATION METRICS
pmc-10739432.creator: Michael Pervratil, Dorota Kossowska-Kuhn, Neil Charness
pmc-10739432.description: Being able to navigate one’s environment is a critical skill that contributes to daily living in a variety of circumstances. Navigation is also a complex skill, composed of multiple subskills that play a part in overall performance. Along with other facets of cognition, navigation ability is expected to decline as a part of normal aging processes.

pmc-12489418.title: Acute Next-Day Effects of Alcohol Use on Daily Cognitive Functioning Among Young Adults: Protocol for a 21-Day Diary Study
pmc-12489418.creator: Ashley N Linden-Carmichael, Jacqueline Mogle, Sara E Miller, Jennifer L Shipley, Stephen J Wilson
pmc-12489418.description: BackgroundYoung adults exhibit the highest rates of binge drinking and heavy alcohol use of any age group. Blackout drinking, or alcohol-induced memory loss, is a negative consequence of heavy drinking and is common among young adults. Alcohol use has been found to affect postintoxication cognitive functioning, especially among those who have experienced blackout drinking.

pmc-13281329.creator: Svetlana Novikova, Shyryn Kenzhebekova, Maksat Faizulla, Abdurashid Mussayev, Nail Khissamutdinov, Zhuldyz Nurmykhametova, Yuriy Pya

pmc-13328950.title: Explainable AI for Equitable Nurse Scheduling: Pragmatic Pre-Post Implementation Study
pmc-13328950.creator: Ben-Chang Shia, Szu-Ming Peng, Qui-Yang Zhang, Chiung-Yun Lo, Sheng-Ru Wang, Elizabeth Borycki
pmc-13328950.description: BackgroundInequitable and time-consuming shift scheduling contributes to nurse burnout, dissatisfaction, and turnover. In Taiwan, annual nurse turnover reaches 11.6%, with rigid 3-shift systems and unfair workload distribution frequently cited as key drivers. Although artificial intelligence (AI) scheduling tools exist, most lack transparency and do not formally address algorithmic bias, limiting clinical adoption.

pmc-13380578.title: Effects of anthropometry, age and sex on center of pressure displacement evoked by small trunk perturbations in balance tests
pmc-13380578.creator: Maria Paterna, Francesca Alba, Emiliano Bottoni, Carlo De Benedictis, Daniela Maffiodo, Walter Franco, Zeevi Dvir, Carlo Ferraresi, Silvestro Roatta
pmc-13380578.description: PurposeBalance control can be evaluated by studying the displacement of the center of pressure (CoP) during dynamic posturographic trials. However, differences in anthropometric characteristics may affect the measurement and increase intersubject variability, possibly leading to misinterpretation. This study evaluates how sex, age, and anthropometric characteristics (weight, height, and foot length) influence the CoP displacement to postural perturbations.

pmc-13458044.title: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence-deep learning-based cine short-axis segmentation and manual post-processing for left ventricular function and structure in cardiac magnetic resonance
pmc-13458044.creator: Yanghao Lin, Wenwei Zhong, Junfeng Yao, Jinliang Zeng, Zheng Zhong, Qimin Li, Ting Song
pmc-13458044.description: BackgroundCardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference standard for evaluating left ventricular (LV) function and structure. Manual post-processing is time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited in reproducibility. Deep learning-based artificial intelligence (AI-DL) offers automated image segmentation with expert-level accuracy, but requires clinical validation against manual analysis.

pmc-13534214.title: Essential oils compromise tegumental integrity in Sparicotyle chrysophrii: Insights from SEM and histological analyses
pmc-13534214.creator: Teresa Pirollo, Perla Tedesco, Andrea Gustinelli, Ana Leon, Oswaldo Palenzuela, Itziar Estensoro, Monica Caffara
pmc-13534214.description: This study investigates the morphological effects of various essential oils (EOs) on the monogenean Sparicotyle chrysophrii, a major gill parasite of gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata), through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and histological analyses. Adult parasites obtained from experimental infections were exposed in vitro to different EOs at concentrations ranging from 62.5 to 500 ppm.

pmc-13563687.title: Unmasking Orbital Myopathy: When Enlarged Extraocular Muscles Indicate More Than Thyroid Eye Disease: Report of Two Cases
pmc-13563687.creator: Daisuke Shinohara, Muhammad Abumanhal, Yasuhiro Takahashi, Karuna Sharma
pmc-13563687.description: IntroductionOrbital myopathy is a condition involving the extraocular muscles, and establishment of a differential diagnosis is crucial to determine its etiology. However, the broad spectrum of the etiologies and the overlap in their clinical and radiological findings often make the diagnosis challenging. We report two cases of orbital myopathy that clinically mimicked thyroid eye disease (TED).

pmc-13659333.title: Not only as a Cullin3 ligase adaptor, SPOP may also act as a molecular bridge
pmc-13659333.creator: Yidong Ge, Lili Kong, Yuxuan Li, Xiaofeng Jin
pmc-13659333.description: Speckle-type POZ protein (SPOP), a substrate-binding adaptor of the Cullin3/RING-box1 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, induces degradative or non-degradative ubiquitination of substrates, playing a vital role in various signaling pathways, including androgen receptor (AR)/estrogen receptor (ER)-associated signal transduction, DNA damage response, and immunity.
